sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Perth Amboy?
sections.html:
Perth Amboy has its own sale rule: a Certificate of Code Compliance must be in hand before a house is transferred, whether the buyer pays cash or finances. That single step shapes timing, repairs and who takes on what, so deal with it before a listing goes live.

About 56,739 people lived in the city by the mid-2025 estimate, on 4.66 square miles of land. The fee schedule in the city code covers everything from one-family homes to four-family buildings. The median owned home is valued at $370,600, and Victorian houses on the hills above the waterfront sit alongside many multi-unit buildings.

sections.h2: What the Certificate of Code Compliance requires
sections.html:
Chapter 181 of the city code bars any transfer, conveyance or sale of a residential, commercial or industrial building until the Department of Code Enforcement issues the certificate. The inspection checks zoning, the fire safety code and substantial conformity with the property maintenance code.

The code gives sellers several ways to keep a closing on schedule:

  • A conditional certificate can run 45 days, and the Director may grant a second 45 days on request.
  • A buyer who says in writing that the purchase is as-is can receive a temporary, nonrenewable certificate good for up to six months from transfer, unless a life-safety hazard exists.
  • A certificate may issue even when the building falls short of full code compliance, provided it is in substantial compliance and safe, sound and sturdy.
  • A denial can be appealed in writing within 10 days to a three-member Certificate of Code Compliance Appeals Board.

Some transfers are exempt, including those between immediate family members, transfers through probate, sales of a building inspected or certified within the previous six months, and purchases made to demolish the building. Violations carry a fine up to $1,000, jail up to 90 days, or both, with each day counted separately. The code also lists a $25 per unit residential reinspection fee and exempts holders of a senior citizen property tax exemption from the fees. Call Code Enforcement for the current inspection charges.

Most Perth Amboy homes are rentals. Only 35.4 percent are occupied by their owners, median gross rent is $1,688 and median household income is $61,977.

A buyer of a tenant-occupied building steps into the city's rent control ordinance, Chapter 353, which a Rent Leveling Board enforces. Since November 1, 2022, increases are capped at 3 percent where water is included in rent and 2.5 percent where it is not. Periodic tenants on terms shorter than a year cannot be charged an increase until the tenancy passes twelve months. Anyone pricing a sale on rent growth should work from those caps.

With 83.6 percent of residents Hispanic or Latino and 79.5 percent of those aged five and up speaking another language at home, many sellers and tenants read Spanish first. The city posts its rent control information in English and Spanish, and a seller who does the same with notices will answer questions sooner.

They can affect a sale if the building stands in or beside a historic district. The Historic Preservation Commission, formed in 1993, reviews proposed changes to designated sites and structures and new construction within or next to districts, under Chapter 258 of the city code.

The historic waterfront neighborhood holds much of the old building stock, including the Proprietary House built in 1764 as a royal governor's residence, and Market Square across from City Hall. A buyer planning exterior changes in that area should expect commission review, so mention it up front when you market the house. If you are unsure whether your parcel sits in or next to a district, ask the city before you list, since a buyer's attorney will raise the same question during due diligence.

sections.h2: How are the deed and the taxes handled for a Perth Amboy sale?
sections.html:
The assessor's office maintains files on over 9,500 parcels and reviews each transfer. Request a tax search and payoff from the Tax Collection office ahead of closing, and confirm the city has your current mailing address.

Deeds for Perth Amboy parcels go to the Middlesex County Clerk's registry in New Brunswick, where walk-in filers must arrive by 4 p.m. on weekdays. A paper deed without its cover sheet draws a $20 indexing charge, and title agents can skip the counter by filing electronically.

If the house sits in an estate, the executor signs the seller's Gross Income Tax form on the estate's behalf, and the city's code exempts probate transfers from the compliance certificate. Heirs who sell after taking title sign for themselves, using the form that matches their own residency. The seller also pays the state realty transfer fee at recording, set by bracket on the sale price.

sections.h2: Order of steps for a Perth Amboy sale
sections.html:
Start with Code Enforcement. Ask whether your transfer is exempt, for example a family or probate transfer, or a building inspected or certified in the previous six months. If it is not exempt, request the inspection early enough that a conditional certificate of 45 days, with one more 45-day extension, covers any repairs.

Next, line up the paperwork a buyer will ask for: leases, security deposit records and the rent level for each unit if tenants are in place. Then order the tax search and payoff, and have your attorney or title agent prepare the deed and the state tax forms. If the inspection is denied, remember you have 10 days to appeal in writing.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer help a Perth Amboy seller?
sections.html:
A cash offer helps when the building would fail the code inspection, carries tenants a seller no longer wants to manage, or must close before a conditional certificate runs out. In each case the as-is certificate route can let the buyer take the repairs after closing.

Ask any buyer whether the offer assumes the temporary certificate, who pays for inspections, and how existing leases and security deposits will be handled. Compare offers by net proceeds, not by the top-line price. A buyer who will keep tenants needs the rent cap history, while a buyer who will demolish may qualify for the demolition exemption, so ask what the plan is.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate to sell a house in Perth Amboy?
faqs.a: Yes. Chapter 181 of the city code requires a Certificate of Code Compliance before a residential or commercial building is transferred, for cash and financed sales alike.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Perth Amboy house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, with limits. If the buyer states in writing that the purchase is as-is, the city can issue a temporary, nonrenewable certificate for up to six months, unless a life-safety condition exists.

faqs.q: Are probate and family transfers exempt in Perth Amboy?
faqs.a: Yes. The code exempts transfers between immediate family members and transfers made through probate proceedings from the certificate requirement.

faqs.q: How much can rent rise in a Perth Amboy rental I am selling?
faqs.a: Up to 3 percent a year where water is included and 2.5 percent where it is not, under the rent control cap in force since November 1, 2022.

faqs.q: Where is a Perth Amboy deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Middlesex County Clerk's registry in New Brunswick. Title agents and attorneys can also submit electronically.
